localization.event.mahdist_state.name: Mahdist state in Sudan
localization.event.mahdist_state.desc: Muhammad Ahmad proclaims himself Mahdi and leads a revolt against Turco-Egyptian rule, taking Khartoum (1885, Gordon killed); the Khalifa Abdallahi rules until Kitchener's Anglo-Egyptian army destroys the Mahdist army at Omdurman (1898).
localization.event.samori_toure_resistance.name: Samori Touré's Wassoulou empire
localization.event.samori_toure_resistance.desc: Samori Touré, who built the Wassoulou empire with locally made and imported rifles, fights French expansion for 16 years, moving his entire state eastward before his capture in 1898.
localization.event.anglo_zulu_war.name: Anglo-Zulu War
localization.event.anglo_zulu_war.desc: Britain invades Zululand to advance confederation in South Africa; the Zulu army destroys a British column at Isandlwana but is defeated at Ulundi; the kingdom is partitioned into 13 chiefdoms.
localization.event.south_african_war.name: South African War
localization.event.south_african_war.desc: Britain fights the Transvaal and Orange Free State over gold-rich territory; guerrilla war is met with farm burning and concentration camps where about 26,000 Boer women and children and at least 14,000 Black Africans die.
localization.event.rinderpest_epizootic.name: African rinderpest epizootic
localization.event.rinderpest_epizootic.desc: Rinderpest introduced via cattle imported to the Horn kills perhaps 80-90% of cattle across eastern and southern Africa; famine follows (the Ethiopian 'Great Famine' 1888-92).
localization.event.inca_expansion.name: Inca imperial expansion
localization.event.inca_expansion.desc: Under Pachacuti and Topa Inca Yupanqui, Tawantinsuyu conquers the Chimú kingdom (c.1470), the Titicaca basin, Quito and central Chile, governing through the khipu, mit'a labour, storehouses (qollqa) and the road network (Qhapaq Ñan); Huayna Capac extends it north.
localization.event.aztec_imperial_height.name: Triple Alliance at its height
localization.event.aztec_imperial_height.desc: Under Ahuitzotl the Triple Alliance extends tribute networks to Soconusco on the Pacific coast and rebuilds the Templo Mayor (1487); Tlaxcala and the Purépecha remain unconquered enemies.
localization.event.columbus_first_voyage.name: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
localization.event.columbus_first_voyage.desc: Sponsored by Castile, Christopher Columbus sails west and lands in the Bahamas (Guanahani, 12 October 1492), Cuba and Hispaniola, meeting Lucayan and Taíno peoples; La Navidad is founded.
localization.event.portuguese_cape_route.name: Portuguese sea route to India
localization.event.portuguese_cape_route.desc: Bartolomeu Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope (1488); Vasco da Gama, guided from Malindi by a Gujarati or Arab pilot, reaches Calicut (1498); Cabral's 1500 fleet touches Brazil.
localization.event.treaty_of_tordesillas.name: Treaty of Tordesillas
localization.event.treaty_of_tordesillas.desc: Castile and Portugal, after papal bulls (1493), divide newly encountered lands along a meridian 370 leagues west of Cape Verde, giving Portugal Brazil's eastern bulge.
localization.event.taino_collapse.name: Collapse of Taíno society
localization.event.taino_collapse.desc: Forced tribute and labour under the encomienda, warfare (Anacaona executed 1503), famine and epidemics (smallpox 1518) devastate the Taíno of Hispaniola, Puerto Rico and Cuba; enslaved Africans are imported from 1501. Resistance includes Hatuey and Enriquillo's revolt (1519-33).
localization.event.spanish_conquest_of_the_aztecs.des: Hernán Cortés's few hundred Spaniards ally with Tlaxcala and other altepetl hostile to the Triple Alliance; Moctezuma II dies in captivity; after a smallpox epidemic and a siege, Tenochtitlan falls to an army that is overwhelmingly Indigenous.
localization.event.inca_civil_war.name: Inca Civil War
localization.event.inca_civil_war.desc: After Huayna Capac dies (c.1527), probably of smallpox that preceded the Spaniards, his sons Huáscar and Atahualpa fight a civil war; Atahualpa wins just as Pizarro arrives.
localization.event.spanish_conquest_of_the_inca.name: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire
localization.event.spanish_conquest_of_the_inca.desc: Francisco Pizarro captures Atahualpa at Cajamarca, takes a ransom room of gold and silver, executes him (1533) and enters Cusco with Indigenous allies; Manco Inca's great rebellion (1536) fails and he retreats to Vilcabamba.
localization.event.new_laws_of_1542.name: New Laws of 1542
localization.event.new_laws_of_1542.desc: Charles V, influenced by Bartolomé de las Casas, bans Indigenous enslavement and restricts encomiendas; encomenderos revolt in Peru (Gonzalo Pizarro), and the inheritance clauses are partly withdrawn (1545). The Valladolid debate follows (1550-51).
localization.event.potosi_silver_discovered.name: Potosí silver and the mita
localization.event.potosi_silver_discovered.desc: The Cerro Rico of Potosí is opened in 1545; Viceroy Toledo introduces mercury amalgamation (with Huancavelica mercury) and reorganises the Inca mit'a into a forced mining draft of about 13,500 men a year (1573).
localization.event.fall_of_vilcabamba.name: Fall of Vilcabamba
localization.event.fall_of_vilcabamba.desc: Viceroy Toledo's forces capture the last Inca stronghold; Túpac Amaru I is executed in Cusco.
localization.event.portuguese_brazil_captaincies.name: Portuguese colonisation of Brazil
localization.event.portuguese_brazil_captaincies.desc: After brazilwood trading, Portugal founds São Vicente (1532), creates hereditary captaincies (1534) and a royal government at Salvador (1549); sugar mills in Pernambuco and Bahia use enslaved Indigenous and then mostly African labour. Jesuits gather Tupi peoples into aldeias.
localization.event.jamestown_founded.name: Founding of Jamestown
localization.event.jamestown_founded.desc: The Virginia Company of London plants Jamestown inside Tsenacommacah, the paramount chiefdom of Wahunsenacah (Powhatan). The colony survives the 'Starving Time' (1609-10) only through resupply and seized Powhatan corn; the First Anglo-Powhatan War (1610-14) ends with Pocahontas's marriage to John Rolfe, whose tobacco becomes the export staple. The first recorded Africans arrive in 1619. Opechancanough's coordinated attack of 22 March 1622 kills about 347 colonists.
localization.event.quebec_founded.name: Founding of Quebec
localization.event.quebec_founded.desc: Samuel de Champlain founds a fur-trading post at Quebec on the St Lawrence. To secure the trade he joins the alliance of the Innu (Montagnais), Algonquin and Wendat and fights beside them against the Mohawk at Lake Champlain (1609), binding New France to Indigenous diplomacy and to its partners' war with the Haudenosaunee.
localization.event.dutch_brazil.name: Dutch Brazil and the Pernambucan Insurrection
localization.event.dutch_brazil.desc: The Dutch West India Company (WIC), at war with the Iberian Union, briefly holds Salvador (1624-25), then takes Olinda and Recife (1630) and the sugar captaincies of the northeast. Under Johan Maurits of Nassau-Siegen (1637-44) New Holland allies with Tarairiu (Tapuia) people under Janduí and seizes Elmina (1637) and Luanda (1641) to supply enslaved Africans. Luso-Brazilian planters rise in 1645; with troops led by the Potiguar commander Felipe Camarão and the Black commander Henrique Dias they win at Guararapes (1648, 1649) and force the Dutch to capitulate at Taborda in 1654. The Treaty of The Hague (1661) confirms Portuguese possession for an indemnity.
localization.event.sugar_revolution_barbados.name: Sugar revolution in Barbados
localization.event.sugar_revolution_barbados.desc: English settlers on Barbados (from 1627) turn from tobacco and cotton to sugar in the 1640s, adopting cane, mills and credit partly from Dutch merchants and Pernambuco. Large planters buy out smallholders and replace indentured servants with enslaved Africans, who form the majority of the population by the 1660s; the Barbados slave code of 1661 becomes a model for Jamaica, Antigua and South Carolina. Mortality is so high that the enslaved population is kept up only by continuing imports. Plots by the enslaved are uncovered in 1675 and 1692 and punished with mass executions.
localization.event.palmares_quilombo.name: Quilombo dos Palmares
localization.event.palmares_quilombo.desc: People escaping Pernambuco's sugar plantations build mocambos in the Serra da Barriga hills. Palmares grows during the Dutch war into a confederation of fortified villages under a king, Ganga Zumba, at the capital Macaco, farming, trading with neighbouring settlers and repelling repeated Dutch and Portuguese expeditions. In 1678 Ganga Zumba accepts a treaty granting freedom and land at Cucaú in return for handing back new fugitives; Zumbi rejects it and leads continued resistance. Paulista bandeirantes under Domingos Jorge Velho take Macaco in 1694, and Zumbi is killed on 20 November 1695.
localization.event.conquest_of_peten_itza.name: Fall of Nojpetén and the Itza kingdom
localization.event.conquest_of_peten_itza.desc: The Itza kingdom, ruled from the island capital Nojpetén in Lake Petén Itzá, kept its independence for 170 years after Cortés passed through in 1525, turning away Franciscan missions and killing missionaries and soldiers in the 1620s. In 1695-96 the friar Andrés de Avendaño reaches Nojpetén and the ruler Ajaw Kan Ek' sends envoys to Mérida offering submission, but rival Itza leaders and the Kowoj oppose him and Spanish parties are attacked. Governor Martín de Urzúa y Arizmendi of Yucatán builds a road through the forest and a galley on the lake, and storms Nojpetén on 13 March 1697.
localization.event.pontiacs_war.name: Pontiac's War
localization.event.pontiacs_war.desc: After France gives up its claims, General Amherst cuts the diplomatic gifts and ammunition the Great Lakes and Ohio nations expected, while settlers press into the Ohio country. Drawing on the Lenape prophet Neolin's call to reject dependence on Europeans, Odawa, Ojibwe, Potawatomi, Wyandot, Seneca, Lenape, Shawnee, Miami and other nations, with the Odawa war leader Pontiac prominent, besiege Detroit and Fort Pitt and capture or force the abandonment of most British posts west of Niagara. The Royal Proclamation of 7 October 1763 reserves lands west of the Appalachian divide for Indigenous nations; Sir William Johnson makes peace in 1764-66, restoring gift diplomacy.
localization.event.american_revolution.name: American Revolution
localization.event.american_revolution.desc: Colonial resistance to parliamentary taxation and the Coercive Acts (1774) becomes war at Lexington and Concord; the Continental Congress declares independence on 4 July 1776. After Saratoga (1777) France allies with the United States (1778), Spain joins the war against Britain (1779) and Britain fights the Dutch Republic (1780); Yorktown (1781) ends major fighting and the Treaty of Paris (1783) recognises independence with a western border on the Mississippi. The Haudenosaunee confederacy splits: most Mohawk, Seneca, Cayuga and Onondaga fight for Britain under leaders such as Joseph Brant, Oneida and Tuscarora for the Patriots, and the Sullivan-Clinton campaign (1779) burns dozens of Haudenosaunee towns. Tens of thousands of enslaved people escape to British lines after Dunmore's (1775) and the Philipsburg (1779) proclamations; about 3,000 Black Loyalists are evacuated to Nova Scotia.
localization.event.tupac_amaru_rebellion.name: Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II and Túpac Katari
localization.event.tupac_amaru_rebellion.desc: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, a kuraka of Tinta province who claimed descent from the last Inca, takes the name Túpac Amaru II, seizes and executes the corregidor Antonio de Arriaga and calls Indigenous, mestizo and some creole subjects to end the forced sale of goods (reparto), the mita and abusive officials, at first in the king's name. With Micaela Bastidas directing supply and command, his forces win at Sangarará but fail to take Cusco; he is captured and executed in Cusco on 18 May 1781 with Bastidas and relatives. The war continues under Diego Cristóbal Túpac Amaru and, in Upper Peru, under Túpac Katari and Bartolina Sisa, whose Aymara forces besiege La Paz for months in 1781; it ends in 1782-83 amid massacres and reprisals on both sides.
localization.event.haitian_revolution.name: Haitian Revolution
localization.event.haitian_revolution.desc: In Saint-Domingue, the most profitable plantation colony in the world with about half a million enslaved people, the enslaved of the Northern Plain rise in August 1791 after the Bois Caïman gathering. Facing the insurgents, Spain and Britain, the commissioner Sonthonax abolishes slavery in the north (1793) and the French Convention abolishes it throughout the empire (4 February 1794). Toussaint Louverture, a formerly enslaved general, defeats British and rival forces and issues a constitution (1801). Napoleon sends Leclerc's expedition (1802) to restore French control and, as in Guadeloupe, slavery; Toussaint is deported and dies in France, but Jean-Jacques Dessalines unites Black and mixed-race forces, wins at Vertières (18 November 1803) and declares Haiti independent on 1 January 1804. In early 1804 most remaining French colonists are killed on Dessalines's orders.
localization.event.louisiana_purchase.name: Louisiana Purchase
localization.event.louisiana_purchase.desc: Spain had secretly returned Louisiana to France (San Ildefonso, 1800). With Leclerc's army destroyed in Saint-Domingue and war with Britain about to resume, Napoleon sells the French claim to the western Mississippi basin and New Orleans to the United States for about 15 million dollars, by a treaty signed in Paris on 30 April 1803. Almost all of the territory is held by Indigenous nations such as the Osage, Pawnee, Lakota and Cheyenne; the United States buys a European claim, not control.
localization.event.latin_american_independence.name: Spanish American wars of independence
localization.event.latin_american_independence.desc: After Napoleon deposes the Spanish Bourbons, juntas govern in the name of Ferdinand VII in Caracas, Buenos Aires, Bogotá and Santiago (1810), while in New Spain the priest Miguel Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores (16 September 1810) launches a mass insurgency of Indigenous and mestizo villagers, continued by José María Morelos. Ferdinand's restoration (1814) brings repression. Simón Bolívar, aided by Haiti's president Alexandre Pétion on condition that he free the enslaved, and José de San Martín, who crosses the Andes in 1817, lead armies that depend on llanero, pardo, Indigenous and formerly enslaved soldiers. Mexico becomes independent through Iturbide's Plan of Iguala (1821); Ayacucho (9 December 1824) ends Spanish rule on the South American mainland, and the last royalist garrison at Callao surrenders in January 1826.
localization.event.brazilian_independence.name: Brazilian independence
localization.event.brazilian_independence.desc: Fleeing Napoleon's invasion, the Portuguese court reaches Brazil in 1808, opens its ports to friendly nations and makes Rio de Janeiro the seat of the monarchy, raised to a kingdom united with Portugal in 1815. When the liberal revolution of 1820 forces João VI home (1821) and the Lisbon Cortes tries to reduce Brazil's status, the prince regent Pedro refuses to leave (Dia do Fico, 9 January 1822), declares independence on 7 September 1822 and is acclaimed emperor. The war against Portuguese garrisons, fought in Bahia with Black, mestizo and Indigenous volunteers, ends on 2 July 1823; Portugal recognises independence in 1825 after British mediation and an indemnity.
localization.event.baptist_war.name: Baptist War in Jamaica
localization.event.baptist_war.desc: Led by Samuel Sharpe, an enslaved Baptist deacon, enslaved people in western Jamaica plan a sit-down strike after Christmas 1831 to demand wages and freedom; it becomes the largest slave rising in the British Caribbean, with estates burned across St James and neighbouring parishes. Militia and troops crush it within weeks; about 14 whites are killed, while hundreds of rebels are killed in the fighting or executed afterwards, Sharpe among them (May 1832).
localization.event.british_emancipation.name: Abolition of slavery in the British Empire
localization.event.british_emancipation.desc: After the Demerara (1823) and Jamaica (1831-32) risings, mass petitioning and the 1832 Reform Act, Parliament passes the Slavery Abolition Act (1833). From 1 August 1834 about 800,000 enslaved people in the Caribbean, the Cape, Mauritius and British Guiana become 'apprentices' still bound to unpaid labour; protests and strikes (notably in Trinidad in 1834) and renewed campaigning end apprenticeship everywhere on 1 August 1838. Slaveholders receive 20 million pounds compensation; the formerly enslaved receive nothing.
localization.event.indian_removal_act.name: Indian Removal and the Trail of Tears
localization.event.indian_removal_act.desc: President Andrew Jackson signs the Indian Removal Act. The Choctaw (from 1831), Muscogee (Creek, 1836), Chickasaw (1837) and Cherokee (1838-39) are forced west of the Mississippi to Indian Territory; tens of thousands die or suffer on the marches and in camps. The Cherokee Nation resists through its constitution, press and the courts, winning Worcester v. Georgia (1832), which Jackson does not enforce; Principal Chief John Ross petitions against the minority Treaty of New Echota (1835). The Seminole fight the Second Seminole War (1835-42) and some remain in Florida.
localization.event.mexican_american_war.name: Mexican-American War
localization.event.mexican_american_war.desc: After the US annexes Texas (1845) and sends troops into the disputed land south of the Nueces, fighting begins; US armies take California and New Mexico, and Winfield Scott lands at Veracruz and occupies Mexico City (September 1847). By the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo Mexico cedes about half its territory, from California to New Mexico, for 15 million dollars. Years of Comanche and Apache raiding had already devastated Mexico's northern states.
localization.event.caste_war_of_yucatan.name: Caste War of Yucatán
localization.event.caste_war_of_yucatan.desc: Maya peasants of eastern and southern Yucatán, led by Cecilio Chi and Jacinto Pat and angered by land loss to sugar and henequen estates, taxes and church fees, rise in 1847 and by 1848 nearly drive the creole elite to Mérida and Campeche; Yucatán's governor even offers sovereignty to the US, Britain or Spain. Pushed back, the rebels found Chan Santa Cruz around the cult of the Speaking Cross (1850), an independent Maya polity that trades arms with British Honduras until Mexican troops take it in 1901.
localization.event.brazilian_end_of_slave_trade.name: Brazil ends the slave trade
localization.event.brazilian_end_of_slave_trade.desc: Brazil's 1831 law banning slave imports is ignored and hundreds of thousands of Africans are landed illegally, mostly from West Central Africa. Fear of revolt after the 1835 Malê uprising of enslaved Muslims in Salvador, British pressure under the Aberdeen Act (1845) and Royal Navy raids on slavers in Brazilian ports in 1850 lead the imperial government to pass and enforce the Eusébio de Queirós Law; the last known landings occur in the mid-1850s.
localization.event.us_civil_war.name: American Civil War and emancipation
localization.event.us_civil_war.desc: After Abraham Lincoln's election on a platform against slavery's expansion, eleven slave states secede and form the Confederacy; the war begins at Fort Sumter. Enslaved people flee to Union lines in their hundreds of thousands, forcing the issue of emancipation; the Emancipation Proclamation (1 January 1863) frees those in rebel areas and opens the army to Black men, about 180,000 of whom serve. The Confederacy surrenders in April 1865 and the Thirteenth Amendment (December 1865) abolishes slavery, freeing about four million people.
localization.event.paraguayan_war.name: Paraguayan War
localization.event.paraguayan_war.desc: When Brazil intervenes in Uruguay's civil war, Paraguay's Francisco Solano López seizes a Brazilian ship, invades Mato Grosso and then Argentine Corrientes; Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay's Colorado government sign the Treaty of the Triple Alliance (May 1865). After the long siege of Humaitá and the fall of Asunción (1869), López is killed at Cerro Corá.
localization.event.end_of_cuban_slave_trade.name: End of the slave trade to Cuba
localization.event.end_of_cuban_slave_trade.desc: Cuba, the world's leading sugar producer, keeps importing enslaved Africans illegally decades after Spain's treaties with Britain (1817, 1835). Planters also bring about 125,000 Chinese indentured labourers (1847-74) under harsh contracts. The 1862 Anglo-American search treaty and the Union's victory remove US-flag cover, and Spain passes a law to repress the trade; the last known slave landing in Cuba is in 1867.
localization.event.war_of_the_pacific.name: War of the Pacific
localization.event.war_of_the_pacific.desc: When Bolivia raises a tax on a Chilean-British nitrate company in its Atacama coast, breaching an 1874 treaty, Chile occupies Antofagasta and declares war on Bolivia and its secret ally Peru. Chile wins command of the sea (capturing the Huáscar at Angamos, October 1879), takes the nitrate provinces and occupies Lima (1881). Andrés Cáceres leads a highland guerrilla resistance with Indigenous peasant fighters. The Treaty of Ancón (1883) gives Chile Tarapacá; a truce (1884) leaves Bolivia without a coast.
localization.event.brazilian_abolition.name: Lei Áurea - abolition of slavery in Brazil
localization.event.brazilian_abolition.desc: After the Rio Branco free-womb law (1871) and the Sexagenarian Law (1885), a mass abolitionist movement, led in part by Black Brazilians such as Luís Gama, André Rebouças and José do Patrocínio, wins abolition in Ceará and Amazonas (1884). In 1887-88 enslaved people leave the São Paulo coffee plantations in mass flights, helped by abolitionists and quilombos such as Jabaquara near Santos, and the army refuses to hunt them. Princess Isabel signs the Golden Law, freeing without compensation the roughly 700,000 people still enslaved.
localization.event.wounded_knee.name: Wounded Knee Massacre
localization.event.wounded_knee.desc: After the US seizes the Black Hills (1877) and breaks up the Great Sioux Reservation (1889), hungry Lakota on shrunken reservations take up the Ghost Dance taught by the Paiute prophet Wovoka. Agents call in the army; Sitting Bull is killed during an arrest (15 December 1890). Spotted Elk's (Big Foot's) Miniconjou band, travelling to Pine Ridge, is surrounded at Wounded Knee Creek by the 7th Cavalry; during disarmament the troops open fire, killing about 250 to 300 Lakota, many of them women and children.
localization.event.spanish_american_war.name: Cuban War of Independence and the Spanish-American War
localization.event.spanish_american_war.desc: Cuban insurgents organised by José Martí's Cuban Revolutionary Party and led by Máximo Gómez and Antonio Maceo, a multiracial army with many Afro-Cuban officers, rise in 1895; Spain's General Weyler herds rural civilians into reconcentration camps where very many die. After the USS Maine explodes in Havana harbour (February 1898) the US declares war, destroys Spanish fleets at Manila Bay and Santiago and, by the Treaty of Paris, takes Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines while Cuba is placed under US occupation. The Platt Amendment (1901) makes the Cuban republic of 1902 a US protectorate.
localization.event.panama_canal.name: Panamanian secession and the Panama Canal
localization.event.panama_canal.desc: After a French company under Ferdinand de Lesseps fails (1881-89) with very heavy deaths from yellow fever and malaria, the Colombian Senate rejects the Hay-Herrán Treaty. Panamanian separatists declare independence with US warships blocking Colombian troops, and the Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty gives the US a canal zone in perpetuity. William Gorgas's mosquito control ends yellow fever on the isthmus; tens of thousands of workers, most from the British Caribbean (especially Barbados and Jamaica), dig the canal under a segregated 'gold roll'/'silver roll' pay system. The canal opens on 15 August 1914.
localization.event.mexican_revolution.name: Mexican Revolution
localization.event.mexican_revolution.desc: Francisco Madero's call to revolt against Porfirio Díaz's long rule brings down the regime (May 1911). Emiliano Zapata's villagers in Morelos demand land under the Plan de Ayala (1911); Madero is murdered in Victoriano Huerta's coup (1913), and Constitutionalists under Venustiano Carranza, Pancho Villa's Division of the North and the Zapatistas defeat Huerta, then fight each other. The US occupies Veracruz (1914) and sends Pershing after Villa (1916-17). The 1917 Constitution promises land reform, labour rights and national ownership of subsoil resources; Álvaro Obregón takes power in 1920.
localization.event.kazakh_khanate_founded.name: Founding of the Kazakh Khanate
localization.event.kazakh_khanate_founded.desc: Janibek and Kerei, Chinggisid sultans, break with Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek confederation and lead their followers to the Chu valley, founding the Kazakh Khanate.
Muhammad Shaybani Khan takes Samarkand (1500), defeats Babur, and conquers Herat (1507), ending Timurid rule in Central Asia; he dies fighting Shah Ismail at Merv (1510).
localization.event.sikh_panth_founded.name: Guru Nanak and the Sikh Panth
localization.event.sikh_panth_founded.desc: Guru Nanak preaches devotion to one formless God, rejection of caste ritualism and community kitchens (langar), founding the community at Kartarpur; nine successor Gurus follow.
localization.event.portuguese_goa.name: Portuguese capture of Goa
localization.event.portuguese_goa.desc: Afonso de Albuquerque takes Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate, making it the capital of the Estado da Índia; Hormuz (1515) and Malacca (1511) complete the chokepoint strategy. Earlier Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (1498) and Portugal fought the Mamluk-Gujarati fleet at Diu (1509).
localization.event.first_battle_of_panipat.name: First Battle of Panipat
localization.event.first_battle_of_panipat.desc: Babur, ruler of Kabul, uses field artillery and a wagon laager to defeat Ibrahim Lodi's much larger army; he then defeats the Rajput confederacy under Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527).
localization.event.akbar_consolidation.name: Akbar's consolidation of the Mughal Empire
localization.event.akbar_consolidation.desc: Akbar wins the Second Battle of Panipat (1556), builds the mansabdari rank system and zabt land revenue (Todar Mal), allies with Rajput houses through marriage and office, abolishes the jizya (1564) and promotes sulh-i kul (universal peace) among religions.
localization.event.battle_of_talikota.name: Battle of Talikota
localization.event.battle_of_talikota.desc: An alliance of the Deccan sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar) defeats Vijayanagara; its capital is sacked and abandoned.
localization.event.khalsa_founded.name: Founding of the Khalsa
localization.event.khalsa_founded.desc: Guru Gobind Singh initiates the Khalsa at Anandpur on Vaisakhi, a community of initiated Sikhs with distinct identity and martial obligations, after the Mughal execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur (1675).
localization.event.shivaji_coronation.name: Shivaji's coronation
localization.event.shivaji_coronation.desc: After decades of guerrilla war against Bijapur and the Mughals from hill forts in the western Deccan, Shivaji Bhonsle is crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad.
localization.event.death_of_aurangzeb.name: Death of Aurangzeb and the Mughal succession crisis
localization.event.death_of_aurangzeb.desc: Aurangzeb dies at Ahmednagar after 25 years of Deccan wars; succession wars follow and provincial governors (Hyderabad, Bengal, Awadh) become autonomous within decades.
localization.event.durrani_empire_founded.name: Founding of the Durrani Empire
localization.event.durrani_empire_founded.desc: After Nader Shah's assassination, the Abdali (Durrani) Pashtun leader Ahmad Shah is chosen at a jirga in Kandahar; he builds an empire from Khorasan to Punjab and Kashmir through repeated invasions of India.
localization.event.battle_of_plassey.name: Battle of Plassey and the Company's diwani
localization.event.battle_of_plassey.desc: Robert Clive's East India Company force defeats Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula after bribing his commander Mir Jafar; after Buxar (1764) the Mughal emperor grants the Company the diwani (revenue rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa (Treaty of Allahabad 1765).
localization.event.third_battle_of_panipat.name: Third Battle of Panipat
localization.event.third_battle_of_panipat.desc: Ahmad Shah Durrani, allied with the Rohillas and Awadh, defeats the Maratha army under Sadashivrao Bhau; tens of thousands of soldiers and camp followers are killed.
localization.event.bengal_famine_1770.name: Great Bengal Famine of 1770
localization.event.bengal_famine_1770.desc: Drought and crop failure in Bengal and Bihar, worsened by Company revenue collection that was maintained or increased, kill an estimated several million people (contemporary claim of one-third of the population).
localization.event.anglo_mysore_wars.name: Anglo-Mysore Wars
localization.event.anglo_mysore_wars.desc: Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan's Mysore, with French support, rocket artillery and a reformed army, fight four wars against the East India Company and its allies; Tipu dies defending Seringapatam (1799).
localization.event.sikh_empire_founded.name: Ranjit Singh's Sikh Empire
localization.event.sikh_empire_founded.desc: Ranjit Singh takes Lahore (1799), unites the Sikh misls, builds a European-trained Khalsa army and conquers Multan, Kashmir and Peshawar; after his death (1839) the empire is annexed by the British following two Anglo-Sikh wars.
localization.event.third_anglo_maratha_war.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
localization.event.third_anglo_maratha_war.desc: The Company defeats the Peshwa and the Maratha chiefs (Holkar, Bhonsle); the Peshwa's territories are annexed and other Maratha rulers become princely states.
localization.event.first_anglo_afghan_war.name: First Anglo-Afghan War
localization.event.first_anglo_afghan_war.desc: Fearing Russian influence, Britain invades Afghanistan to install Shah Shuja; an uprising in Kabul leads to the retreat and destruction of the British-Indian army (1842).
localization.event.indian_rebellion_of_1857.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
localization.event.indian_rebellion_of_1857.desc: Sepoys mutiny at Meerut and march on Delhi, proclaiming Bahadur Shah Zafar emperor; rebellion spreads across north and central India (Lakshmibai of Jhansi, Nana Sahib, Begum Hazrat Mahal) and is crushed with mass reprisals. The Company is abolished and the Crown rules India directly.
localization.event.russian_conquest_of_central_asia.d: Russia absorbs the Kazakh steppe, takes Tashkent (1865), makes Bukhara (1868) and Khiva (1873) protectorates, annexes Kokand (1876) and crushes the Turkmen at Geok Tepe (1881).
localization.event.anglo_russian_convention.name: Anglo-Russian Convention
localization.event.anglo_russian_convention.desc: Britain and Russia divide Iran into spheres of influence, recognise Afghanistan as a British sphere and Tibet as Chinese, without consulting Iran or Afghanistan.
localization.event.tasman_voyages.name: Tasman's voyages and the meeting at Mohua
localization.event.tasman_voyages.desc: Sent from Batavia by Governor-General Anthony van Diemen to find a southern continent and a route east, Abel Tasman's Heemskerck and Zeehaen reach Tasmania (November 1642) and the west coast of Aotearoa (13 December). At anchor off Wharewharangi in Mohua (Golden Bay), the ships are approached by waka of Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri; conch or trumpet calls are exchanged in the evening, and next morning a waka rams a ship's boat and four Dutch sailors are killed. Tasman names the place Murderers' Bay and sails on without landing, reaching Tonga, where Tongans trade peacefully, and Fiji before returning to Batavia (June 1643). A second voyage (1644) charts the north coast of Australia.
localization.event.mendana_voyages.name: Mendaña's voyages to the Solomon Islands and the Marquesas
localization.event.mendana_voyages.desc: Álvaro de Mendaña sails from Callao (November 1567) and reaches Santa Isabel (February 1568), naming the islands after Solomon in hope of gold. Over six months on Santa Isabel, Guadalcanal and Makira, Spanish demands for food, kidnappings and shootings meet armed resistance; islanders kill a Spanish watering party on Guadalcanal and the Spanish burn villages in reprisal. In 1595 Mendaña returns with about 400 settlers, including his wife Isabel Barreto, and the pilot Pedro Fernández de Quirós. In the Marquesas (July 1595) soldiers shoot islanders repeatedly; Quirós put the dead at about 200. At Graciosa Bay on Nendö (Santa Cruz Islands) a settlement is founded, the friendly chief Malope is murdered by Spanish soldiers, and islanders attack the camp; Mendaña dies in October, and Isabel Barreto leads the survivors to Manila (February 1596).
localization.event.jesuits_at_the_ming_court.name: Matteo Ricci and the Jesuits in Beijing
localization.event.jesuits_at_the_ming_court.desc: After nearly twenty years of study and work in Macau, Zhaoqing, Shaozhou, Nanchang and Nanjing, the Jesuit Matteo Ricci and Diego de Pantoja reach Beijing in January 1601 with gifts for the Wanli Emperor, including clocks. They are allowed to stay with an imperial stipend, though Ricci never meets the emperor. Presenting Christianity in the language of Confucian learning, Ricci befriends scholar-officials; with Xu Guangqi he translates the first six books of Euclid (1607), and his world map (1602) is printed and copied. When he dies in 1610 the emperor grants land for his burial in Beijing.
localization.event.afaqi_khojas_and_the_yarkent_khana: Afaq Khoja and the Dzungar conquest of Altishahr

In the Yarkent Khanate, the Chagatayid khans' authority is eroded by rival Naqshbandi Sufi lineages, the Afaqi (White Mountain) and Ishaqi (Black Mountain) khojas. Ismail Khan, a patron of the Ishaqis, expels Afaq Khoja (Hidayat Allah) from Kashgar. Afaq seeks outside help, according to tradition through the Fifth Dalai Lama, and the Dzungar ruler Galdan invades in 1680, takes Yarkent and Kashgar, carries Ismail Khan off to Ili and puts Altishahr under Dzungar tribute. Afaq and his descendants rule as Dzungar clients beside or in place of nominal khans until Afaq's death (1694), after which khoja factions keep fighting under Dzungar overlordship.
localization.event.tumu_crisis.name: Tumu Crisis
localization.event.tumu_crisis.desc: The Zhengtong Emperor leads a poorly prepared campaign against the Oirat leader Esen and is captured at Tumu; Yu Qian defends Beijing and a new emperor is enthroned.
localization.event.onin_war.name: Ōnin War
localization.event.onin_war.desc: A succession dispute in the Ashikaga shogunate and rivalry between the Hosokawa and Yamana destroy Kyoto; shogunal authority collapses and the warring states (Sengoku) era begins.
localization.event.iwami_silver_boom.name: Japanese silver boom
localization.event.iwami_silver_boom.desc: The Iwami Ginzan mine and the cupellation (haifuki) process introduced from Korea (1533) make Japan a major silver producer, perhaps a third of world output in the early 17th century, exported to China via Portuguese, Chinese and Japanese ships.
localization.event.xavier_arrives_in_japan.name: Arrival of Christianity in Japan
localization.event.xavier_arrives_in_japan.desc: Francis Xavier lands at Kagoshima; Portuguese traders (at Tanegashima since 1543, bringing matchlocks) and Jesuits gain converts among daimyo such as Ōmura Sumitada, who opens Nagasaki (1571).
localization.event.imjin_war.name: Imjin War
localization.event.imjin_war.desc: Toyotomi Hideyoshi invades Joseon Korea with about 150,000 troops aiming at Ming China; Korean navy under Yi Sun-sin, righteous armies and Ming intervention force a stalemate; Japan withdraws after Hideyoshi's death.
localization.event.tokugawa_shogunate_established.nam: Battle of Sekigahara and the Tokugawa shogunate
localization.event.tokugawa_shogunate_established.des: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeats the western coalition at Sekigahara and is appointed shogun in 1603, establishing the bakufu at Edo.
localization.event.siege_of_osaka.name: Siege of Osaka
localization.event.siege_of_osaka.desc: The Tokugawa destroy the Toyotomi at Osaka Castle, eliminating the last rival to their rule.
localization.event.sakoku_edicts.name: Sakoku maritime restrictions
localization.event.sakoku_edicts.desc: After banning Christianity (1614) and the Shimabara Rebellion (1637-38), the shogunate bars Japanese from going abroad, expels the Portuguese (1639) and confines Dutch trade to Dejima; trade continues via Chinese merchants, Tsushima-Korea, Satsuma-Ryukyu and Matsumae-Ainu.
localization.event.yermak_conquest_of_sibir.name: Yermak's conquest of the Sibir Khanate
localization.event.yermak_conquest_of_sibir.desc: Cossacks under Yermak, financed by the Stroganov merchants, defeat Khan Kuchum and take Isker; Yermak dies in 1585 but Muscovite forts follow, reaching the Pacific at Okhotsk by 1639.
localization.event.conquest_of_kazan.name: Muscovite conquest of Kazan and Astrakhan
localization.event.conquest_of_kazan.desc: Ivan IV storms Kazan with sappers and artillery (1552) and annexes Astrakhan (1556), giving Muscovy the whole Volga.
localization.event.ming_qing_transition_begins.name: Nurhaci's Seven Grievances
localization.event.ming_qing_transition_begins.desc: Nurhaci, who united the Jurchen tribes and created the banner system, proclaims the Later Jin (1616) and declares war on Ming with the 'Seven Grievances' (1618); Ming defeat at Sarhu (1619) follows.
localization.event.manchu_invasions_of_korea.name: Manchu invasions of Korea
localization.event.manchu_invasions_of_korea.desc: Later Jin invades Joseon in 1627 and, as the Qing, again in 1636; King Injo surrenders at Samjeondo and breaks with the Ming.
localization.event.fall_of_beijing_1644.name: Fall of Beijing and the Qing conquest
localization.event.fall_of_beijing_1644.desc: Li Zicheng's rebel army takes Beijing and the Chongzhen Emperor hangs himself; general Wu Sangui opens the Shanhai Pass to the Manchus, who defeat Li and enthrone the Shunzhi Emperor in Beijing. Southern Ming resistance and massacres (Yangzhou 1645) follow.
localization.event.qing_conquest_of_taiwan.name: Qing conquest of Taiwan
localization.event.qing_conquest_of_taiwan.desc: After suppressing the Revolt of the Three Feudatories (1673-81), Qing admiral Shi Lang defeats the Zheng family's Kingdom of Tungning, which had expelled the Dutch from Taiwan in 1662.
localization.event.treaty_of_nerchinsk.name: Treaty of Nerchinsk
localization.event.treaty_of_nerchinsk.desc: After Qing sieges of Albazin, Russia and the Qing, with Jesuit interpreters, fix the border along the Argun and Stanovoy mountains; Russia withdraws from the Amur.
localization.event.dzungar_genocide.name: Qing destruction of the Dzungar Khanate
localization.event.dzungar_genocide.desc: Exploiting a Dzungar succession war, the Qianlong Emperor conquers the Dzungar Khanate; after Amursana's revolt he orders the extermination of the Dzungars. War, massacre and a smallpox epidemic destroy most of the Dzungar population.
localization.event.canton_system.name: Canton System
localization.event.canton_system.desc: The Qianlong Emperor restricts Western maritime trade to Guangzhou (Canton), conducted through licensed Cohong merchants; tea exports grow while Britain struggles to pay with anything but silver until it turns to Indian opium.
localization.event.macartney_mission.name: Macartney Embassy
localization.event.macartney_mission.desc: Lord Macartney asks the Qianlong Emperor for a permanent embassy and more trading ports; the emperor's edict refuses, stating China has no need of British manufactures.
localization.event.white_lotus_rebellion.name: White Lotus Rebellion
localization.event.white_lotus_rebellion.desc: Millenarian White Lotus sects lead settlers in the Hubei-Sichuan-Shaanxi highlands in revolt against tax extortion; suppression with local militias costs the Qing heavily.
localization.event.first_opium_war.name: First Opium War
localization.event.first_opium_war.desc: After commissioner Lin Zexu destroys British opium at Canton, Britain sends a steam-assisted expedition; the Treaty of Nanjing cedes Hong Kong, opens five ports and imposes an indemnity, followed by extraterritoriality and most-favoured-nation clauses (1843-44).
localization.event.taiping_rebellion.name: Taiping Rebellion
localization.event.taiping_rebellion.desc: Hong Xiuquan, who believed himself Jesus's younger brother, leads the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom from Guangxi to Nanjing (1853); Zeng Guofan's Xiang Army and foreign-officered forces destroy it. Tens of millions die in the war and accompanying famine and epidemics.
localization.event.self_strengthening_movement.name: Self-Strengthening Movement
localization.event.self_strengthening_movement.desc: Officials such as Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang build arsenals, shipyards (Jiangnan, Fuzhou), translation offices and the Beiyang fleet under the slogan 'Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application'.
localization.event.perry_expedition.name: Perry Expedition and the opening of Japan
localization.event.perry_expedition.desc: US Commodore Perry's steam warships force the Convention of Kanagawa (1854); the Harris Treaty (1858) and similar treaties impose open ports, extraterritoriality and fixed tariffs.
localization.event.meiji_restoration.name: Meiji Restoration
localization.event.meiji_restoration.desc: Satsuma and Chōshū samurai, under the slogan of restoring imperial rule, force the last shogun to resign; after the Boshin War the new government abolishes the domains (1871), the samurai class and builds a centralised state.
localization.event.first_sino_japanese_war.name: First Sino-Japanese War
localization.event.first_sino_japanese_war.desc: Japan defeats Qing over influence in Korea; the Treaty of Shimonoseki gives Japan Taiwan and an indemnity and ends Korea's tributary status; the Triple Intervention forces return of Liaodong.
localization.event.boxer_rebellion.name: Boxer Uprising
localization.event.boxer_rebellion.desc: An anti-foreign, anti-Christian movement in Shandong and Zhili besieges the Beijing legations with Qing court backing; an Eight-Nation Alliance captures Beijing; the Boxer Protocol imposes a huge indemnity.
localization.event.russo_japanese_war.name: Russo-Japanese War
localization.event.russo_japanese_war.desc: Japan attacks Port Arthur, wins at Mukden and destroys the Russian Baltic fleet at Tsushima; the Treaty of Portsmouth gives Japan southern Sakhalin, Liaodong and paramountcy in Korea.
localization.event.japanese_annexation_of_korea.name: Japanese annexation of Korea
localization.event.japanese_annexation_of_korea.desc: After making Korea a protectorate (1905) and suppressing the 'righteous armies', Japan annexes Korea outright; colonial rule lasts until 1945 with land surveys, forced assimilation and later forced labour.
localization.event.xinhai_revolution.name: Xinhai Revolution
localization.event.xinhai_revolution.desc: An army mutiny in Wuchang spreads as provinces declare independence; Sun Yat-sen becomes provisional president; Yuan Shikai negotiates the abdication of the last emperor, Puyi.
localization.event.fall_of_constantinople.name: Fall of Constantinople
localization.event.fall_of_constantinople.desc: Mehmed II besieges and storms Constantinople with large cannon and a fleet dragged overland into the Golden Horn; Constantine XI dies in the assault. The city becomes the Ottoman capital.
localization.event.end_of_hundred_years_war.name: End of the Hundred Years' War
localization.event.end_of_hundred_years_war.desc: French artillery wins the Battle of Castillon; England loses Gascony, keeping only Calais (lost 1558).
localization.event.printing_press_spreads.name: Spread of movable-type printing
localization.event.printing_press_spreads.desc: Gutenberg's press at Mainz (c.1450-55) spreads to over 250 European towns by 1500. Movable type existed earlier in China and Korea (Bi Sheng, Goryeo metal type) but alphabetic script made it far cheaper to scale.
localization.event.wars_of_the_roses.name: Wars of the Roses
localization.event.wars_of_the_roses.desc: Dynastic civil wars between Lancaster and York end with Henry Tudor's victory at Bosworth (1485) and Stoke (1487).
localization.event.union_of_castile_and_aragon.name: Union of the crowns of Castile and Aragon
localization.event.union_of_castile_and_aragon.desc: Isabella of Castile marries Ferdinand of Aragon (1469); after the Castilian succession war, both crowns are held jointly from 1479, keeping separate institutions.
localization.event.castile_portugal_union.name: Portuguese succession to Castile (alternative)
localization.event.castile_portugal_union.desc: Afonso V of Portugal claimed Castile through Joanna 'la Beltraneja' in the War of the Castilian Succession and lost. Historical reference for an alternative union.
localization.event.fall_of_granada.name: Conquest of Granada
localization.event.fall_of_granada.desc: Castile and Aragon conquer the Nasrid Emirate of Granada after a ten-year war; Muhammad XII surrenders the Alhambra.
localization.event.alhambra_decree.name: Expulsion of the Jews from Spain
localization.event.alhambra_decree.desc: The Catholic Monarchs order Jews to convert or leave; tens of thousands emigrate (estimates vary widely) to Portugal, North Africa, Italy and the Ottoman Empire. Portugal forces conversion in 1497.
localization.event.italian_wars.name: Italian Wars begin
localization.event.italian_wars.desc: Charles VIII of France invades Italy to claim Naples, starting six decades of French-Habsburg wars in the peninsula.
localization.event.peace_of_cateau_cambresis.name: Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis
localization.event.peace_of_cateau_cambresis.desc: France and Spain end the Italian Wars; Spain dominates Milan, Naples, Sicily and Sardinia.
localization.event.protestant_reformation.name: Protestant Reformation
localization.event.protestant_reformation.desc: Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses at Wittenberg start a challenge to papal authority that spreads through print, princely protection (Saxony) and urban reform movements (Zwingli, later Calvin).
localization.event.german_peasants_war.name: German Peasants' War
localization.event.german_peasants_war.desc: Peasant uprisings across southern and central Germany, demanding (Twelve Articles) relief from serfdom and dues, are crushed; perhaps 100,000 killed.
localization.event.battle_of_mohacs.name: Battle of Mohács and the partition of Hungary
localization.event.battle_of_mohacs.desc: Suleiman's army destroys the Hungarian royal army; King Louis II dies. Hungary is split between Habsburg claimant Ferdinand, John Zápolya and later direct Ottoman rule (Buda 1541).
localization.event.siege_of_vienna_1529.name: First Siege of Vienna
localization.event.siege_of_vienna_1529.desc: Suleiman's siege of Vienna fails due to weather, supply lines and the garrison's defence.
localization.event.english_reformation.name: English Reformation
localization.event.english_reformation.desc: The Act of Supremacy makes Henry VIII head of the Church of England after Rome refuses his annulment; monasteries dissolved 1536-41.
localization.event.council_of_trent.name: Council of Trent
localization.event.council_of_trent.desc: Catholic council defines doctrine against Protestant positions and reforms clergy training (seminaries), launching the Catholic Reformation alongside the Jesuits (approved 1540).
localization.event.peace_of_augsburg.name: Peace of Augsburg
localization.event.peace_of_augsburg.desc: Charles V's brother Ferdinand concludes peace allowing Imperial princes to choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for their lands (later summarised as cuius regio, eius religio); Calvinism excluded.
localization.event.french_wars_of_religion.name: French Wars of Religion
localization.event.french_wars_of_religion.desc: Eight civil wars between Catholics and Huguenots, including the St Bartholomew's Day massacre (1572), end with Henry IV's conversion and the Edict of Nantes (1598).
localization.event.dutch_revolt.name: Dutch Revolt
localization.event.dutch_revolt.desc: Revolt of the Habsburg Netherlands against Philip II's taxation and religious persecution; the northern provinces form the Dutch Republic (Union of Utrecht 1579), recognised at Münster 1648.
localization.event.union_of_lublin.name: Union of Lublin
localization.event.union_of_lublin.desc: Poland and Lithuania convert their personal union into a single Commonwealth with an elective monarchy and shared Sejm.
localization.event.battle_of_lepanto.name: Battle of Lepanto
localization.event.battle_of_lepanto.desc: The Holy League fleet (Spain, Venice, the Papacy and others) destroys the Ottoman galley fleet; the Ottomans rebuild within a year and keep Cyprus.
localization.event.iberian_union.name: Iberian Union
localization.event.iberian_union.desc: After King Sebastian dies at Alcácer Quibir (1578) and Cardinal Henry dies childless, Philip II of Spain takes the Portuguese throne.
localization.event.portuguese_restoration.name: Portuguese Restoration
localization.event.portuguese_restoration.desc: Portuguese nobles proclaim João IV; after a 28-year war Spain recognises independence (Treaty of Lisbon 1668).
localization.event.spanish_armada.name: Spanish Armada
localization.event.spanish_armada.desc: Philip II's fleet fails to escort an invasion army from Flanders to England and is wrecked rounding Scotland and Ireland.
localization.event.time_of_troubles.name: Time of Troubles
localization.event.time_of_troubles.desc: After the Rurikid line ends, famine (1601-03, linked to the Huaynaputina eruption), pretenders, civil war and Polish and Swedish intervention devastate Muscovy until Michael Romanov is elected.
localization.event.thirty_years_war.name: Thirty Years' War
localization.event.thirty_years_war.desc: The Defenestration of Prague starts a Bohemian revolt that grows into a war involving the Emperor, Catholic and Protestant princes, Denmark, Sweden, Spain and France.
localization.event.peace_of_westphalia.name: Peace of Westphalia
localization.event.peace_of_westphalia.desc: Treaties of Münster and Osnabrück end the Thirty Years' War and the Eighty Years' War; Calvinism recognised; Dutch and Swiss independence acknowledged; Sweden and France gain territory.
localization.event.wars_of_the_three_kingdoms.name: Wars of the Three Kingdoms
localization.event.wars_of_the_three_kingdoms.desc: Scottish Bishops' Wars, the Irish rebellion of 1641 and the English Civil War end with Charles I's execution (1649) and Cromwell's conquest of Ireland and Scotland.
localization.event.restoration_of_charles_ii.name: Restoration of the Stuart monarchy
localization.event.restoration_of_charles_ii.desc: After Cromwell's death and the Protectorate's collapse, Parliament restores Charles II.
localization.event.siege_of_vienna_1683.name: Second Siege of Vienna
localization.event.siege_of_vienna_1683.desc: Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa besieges Vienna; a relief army under Jan III Sobieski defeats him at the Kahlenberg. The Holy League war follows.
localization.event.treaty_of_karlowitz.name: Treaty of Karlowitz
localization.event.treaty_of_karlowitz.desc: After the Holy League war the Ottomans cede most of Hungary and Transylvania to the Habsburgs, Podolia to Poland, and the Morea to Venice.
localization.event.glorious_revolution.name: Glorious Revolution
localization.event.glorious_revolution.desc: William of Orange invades England; James II flees; the Bill of Rights limits the crown. War follows in Ireland (Boyne 1690) and Scotland.
localization.event.petrine_reforms.name: Petrine reforms
localization.event.petrine_reforms.desc: Peter I rebuilds the army and navy, creates colleges and the Table of Ranks, subordinates the church and founds St Petersburg (1703).
localization.event.great_northern_war.name: Great Northern War
localization.event.great_northern_war.desc: Russia, Denmark-Norway, Saxony-Poland attack Sweden; Charles XII's victories end at Poltava (1709).
localization.event.treaty_of_nystad.name: Treaty of Nystad
localization.event.treaty_of_nystad.desc: Sweden cedes Livonia, Estonia, Ingria and part of Karelia to Russia; Peter proclaimed Emperor.
localization.event.war_of_the_spanish_succession.name: War of the Spanish Succession
localization.event.war_of_the_spanish_succession.desc: Charles II of Spain dies childless leaving his crowns to Philip of Anjou; a Grand Alliance fights France to prevent Bourbon dominance. Utrecht (1713) keeps Philip V on Spain's throne but separates the crowns; Britain gains Gibraltar, Minorca, Newfoundland and the asiento slave-trade contract.
localization.event.war_of_the_austrian_succession.des: Prussia seizes Silesia from Maria Theresa; war spreads to North America (King George's War) and India (First Carnatic War).
localization.event.seven_years_war.name: Seven Years' War
localization.event.seven_years_war.desc: A global war: Britain and Prussia against France, Austria, Russia and later Spain. Begins in the Ohio valley (1754), fought in Europe, India (Plassey 1757), West Africa and the Caribbean. Treaty of Paris (1763) gives Britain Canada and Florida.
localization.event.partitions_of_poland.name: Partitions of Poland-Lithuania
localization.event.partitions_of_poland.desc: Russia, Prussia and Austria partition the Commonwealth in three stages; the Kościuszko Uprising (1794) is crushed.
localization.event.french_revolution.name: French Revolution
localization.event.french_revolution.desc: Fiscal crisis forces the Estates-General; the National Assembly, storming of the Bastille and abolition of feudal privileges lead to a republic (1792), the Terror and the Directory, ended by Napoleon's coup.
localization.event.french_revolutionary_wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars
localization.event.french_revolutionary_wars.desc: Revolutionary France fights coalitions of monarchies using mass conscription (levée en masse 1793), expands to the Rhine and Italy, and invades Egypt (1798).
localization.event.napoleon_invades_iberia.name: Napoleonic invasion of Iberia
localization.event.napoleon_invades_iberia.desc: France invades Portugal (the royal court flees to Rio de Janeiro) and forces Spain's Bourbons to abdicate (Bayonne 1808); guerrilla war and British intervention follow in the Peninsular War.
localization.event.congress_of_vienna.name: Congress of Vienna
localization.event.congress_of_vienna.desc: After Napoleon's defeat the great powers redraw Europe: restored monarchies, a German Confederation, Russian Poland, a stronger Prussia, and the Concert of Europe; a declaration condemns the slave trade.
localization.event.greek_war_of_independence.name: Greek War of Independence
localization.event.greek_war_of_independence.desc: Greek revolt against Ottoman rule; Egyptian intervention nearly crushes it until Britain, France and Russia destroy the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet at Navarino (1827). Greece is recognised in 1830 (London Protocol).
localization.event.revolutions_of_1848.name: Revolutions of 1848
localization.event.revolutions_of_1848.desc: After harvest failures and a commercial crisis, revolutions break out in Sicily, Paris, Vienna, Berlin, Milan, Budapest and elsewhere; the Frankfurt Parliament fails; most are suppressed by 1849 but serfdom ends in Austria and France gets universal male suffrage.
localization.event.great_irish_famine.name: Great Irish Famine
localization.event.great_irish_famine.desc: Potato blight destroys the staple crop of Ireland's rural poor; with food exports continuing, inadequate relief and mass evictions, about one million die and over one million emigrate.
localization.event.crimean_war.name: Crimean War
localization.event.crimean_war.desc: Russia's pressure on the Ottomans brings Britain, France and Sardinia into war; the siege of Sevastopol ends in Russian defeat. The Peace of Paris neutralises the Black Sea.
localization.event.russian_emancipation_of_serfs.name: Emancipation of the Russian serfs
localization.event.russian_emancipation_of_serfs.desc: Alexander II's manifesto frees about 23 million privately held serfs, who must pay redemption for land allotted through village communes.
localization.event.italian_unification.name: Italian unification
localization.event.italian_unification.desc: Piedmont-Sardinia, allied with France, defeats Austria (1859); Garibaldi's Thousand conquer the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies (1860); the Kingdom of Italy is proclaimed in 1861; Venetia (1866) and Rome (1870) follow.
localization.event.german_unification.name: German unification
localization.event.german_unification.desc: Bismarck's Prussia wins wars against Denmark (1864), Austria (1866) and France (1870-71); the German Empire is proclaimed at Versailles, annexing Alsace-Lorraine.
localization.event.huaynaputina_eruption.name: Eruption of Huaynaputina
localization.event.huaynaputina_eruption.desc: Huaynaputina in southern Peru erupts from 19 February 1600, the largest eruption in recorded South American history (VEI 6). Ash and pyroclastic flows bury villages near Arequipa and ruin the vineyards and farms of the Moquegua valley. Sulphate aerosols cool the Northern Hemisphere: tree-ring series make the summer of 1601 one of the coldest of the last 600 years, and harvests fail across Russia in 1601-03.
localization.event.huaynaputina_eruption.option.hoard: Hoard grain for court and army
localization.event.laki_eruption.name: Laki fissure eruption and the Mist Hardships
localization.event.laki_eruption.desc: The Laki (Lakagígar) fissure in southern Iceland erupts for eight months, releasing about 15 km3 of lava and over 100 million tonnes of sulphur dioxide. Fluorine poisoning and failed hay kill most of Iceland's sheep and about half its cattle and horses; in the ensuing famine (Móðuharðindin, the Mist Hardships) roughly a fifth of Icelanders die. A sulphurous haze covers Europe in summer 1783 and the winter of 1783-84 is exceptionally severe.
localization.event.tambora_eruption.name: Eruption of Tambora and the Year Without a Summer
localization.event.tambora_eruption.desc: Mount Tambora on Sumbawa erupts catastrophically on 10-11 April 1815, the largest eruption in recorded history (VEI 7). The small kingdoms of Tambora and Pekat are destroyed; pyroclastic flows, ashfall, famine and disease kill tens of thousands on Sumbawa and Lombok. Stratospheric aerosols make 1816 the 'Year Without a Summer': June frosts in New England, ruined harvests, dearth and typhus in Switzerland, south-west Germany and Ireland, and a three-year famine in Yunnan.
localization.event.first_cholera_pandemic.name: First cholera pandemic
localization.event.first_cholera_pandemic.desc: Cholera, long endemic in the Ganges delta, breaks out with unusual virulence around Jessore in Bengal in August 1817 and spreads with Company armies (the Marquess of Hastings' field army is struck in November 1817), pilgrims and shipping across India, to Ceylon, Burma, Siam, Java, the Philippines, China (1820) and Japan (1822), and west through the Persian Gulf and Mesopotamia to the Caspian at Astrakhan (1823).
localization.event.industrial_revolution_britain.name: Industrial Revolution
localization.event.industrial_revolution_britain.desc: In Britain, coke-smelted iron (Darby, 1709), Hargreaves's spinning jenny (c.1764), Arkwright's water frame and Cromford mill (1769-71), Crompton's mule (1779), Watt's separate-condenser steam engine (1769, built with Boulton from 1775) and Cort's puddling process (1784) mechanise cotton, iron and power. Factory towns grow around Manchester; the Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens in 1830. Raw cotton increasingly comes from enslaved labour in the US South after the cotton gin (1793), while Indian handloom exports collapse. Belgium, France, the US and Prussia follow; Muhammad Ali's Egypt attempts state-run mills in the 1820s-30s.
localization.event.steamship_era.name: Ocean steam navigation
localization.event.steamship_era.desc: The Sirius and Great Western cross the Atlantic under steam (1838) and Cunard's subsidised mail line opens (1840). The East India Company's iron steamer Nemesis operates on Chinese rivers in the Opium War (1840-42). Screw propellers, iron hulls and Alfred Holt's compound-engined Agamemnon (1866) make long-haul cargo steam economical, and the Suez Canal (1869) gives steamers the route to Asia. By the 1870s most transatlantic migrants travel by steam. Non-European states build their own lines, such as the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Company (1872) and Japan's NYK (1885).
localization.event.telegraph_network.name: Electric telegraph and submarine cables
localization.event.telegraph_network.desc: Cooke and Wheatstone (1837) and Morse (Washington-Baltimore, 1844) create practical electric telegraphs; a Channel cable follows in 1851. The first transatlantic cable (1858) fails within weeks, but the Great Eastern lays a durable one in 1866. Lines and cables, insulated with gutta-percha from Southeast Asian forests, reach India (1870), Australia via Darwin (1871-72), China and Japan (1871), and cross the Pacific (1902-03). Britain dominates the cable industry through private firms such as John Pender's Eastern Telegraph group.
localization.event.second_industrial_revolution.name: Second Industrial Revolution
localization.event.second_industrial_revolution.desc: Bessemer (1856), Siemens-Martin open-hearth and Gilchrist-Thomas basic (1878) processes make cheap steel; dynamos, Edison's Pearl Street power station (1882) and electric motors spread electricity; the German dye and chemical industry (BASF, founded 1865) leads the world; Benz builds a petrol-engined car (1885-86). Germany and the United States overtake Britain in steel. Late industrialisers use the state: Witte's Russia builds the Trans-Siberian Railway (from 1891) and Japan opens the state Yawata steelworks (1901).
localization.event.indian_national_congress_founded.n: Founding of the Indian National Congress
localization.event.indian_national_congress_founded.d: Seventy-two delegates from across British India meet at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay, with W. C. Bonnerjee presiding; Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta and the retired civil servant Allan Octavian Hume help organise it; Surendranath Banerjea's parallel Indian National Conference in Calcutta merges with it in 1886. The early Congress, led by English-educated lawyers, journalists and merchants, petitions for Indian entry to the civil service, legislative representation and lower military spending, and Naoroji develops the 'drain of wealth' critique.
localization.event.oman_zanzibar_split.name: Partition of the Omani sultanate
localization.event.oman_zanzibar_split.desc: Sayyid Said bin Sultan, who had shifted his court from Muscat to Zanzibar and built a clove-plantation and caravan economy on the Swahili coast, dies at sea in October 1856. His sons Majid (in Zanzibar) and Thuwaini (in Muscat) dispute the succession; a Muscat expedition against Zanzibar in 1859 is turned back under British pressure. The arbitration of Lord Canning, Viceroy of India (the Canning Award, 1861), divides the realm into a Sultanate of Zanzibar and a Sultanate of Muscat and Oman, with Zanzibar paying Muscat an annual subsidy.
localization.event.safavid_rise.name: Rise of the Safavids
localization.event.safavid_rise.desc: Ismail, head of the Safavid Sufi order backed by Turkmen Qizilbash tribes, takes Tabriz from the Aq Qoyunlu, is crowned shah and proclaims Twelver Shi'ism the state religion; conquers Iran and Iraq by 1508 and defeats the Uzbeks at Merv (1510).
localization.event.battle_of_chaldiran.name: Battle of Chaldiran
localization.event.battle_of_chaldiran.desc: Selim I's army with artillery and Janissary musketeers defeats Ismail's Qizilbash cavalry and briefly occupies Tabriz; eastern Anatolia passes to the Ottomans.
localization.event.ottoman_conquest_of_mamluks.name: Ottoman conquest of the Mamluk Sultanate
localization.event.ottoman_conquest_of_mamluks.desc: Selim I defeats the Mamluks at Marj Dabiq and Ridaniya, takes Syria, Egypt and the Hejaz; the Ottoman sultan becomes protector of Mecca and Medina.
localization.event.peace_of_amasya.name: Peace of Amasya
localization.event.peace_of_amasya.desc: First formal peace between Suleiman and Tahmasp I after decades of war; Ottomans keep Iraq including Baghdad, Safavids keep Azerbaijan.
localization.event.death_of_suleiman.name: Death of Suleiman the Magnificent
localization.event.death_of_suleiman.desc: Suleiman dies during the siege of Szigetvár; Selim II succeeds with Grand Vizier Sokollu Mehmed governing.
localization.event.battle_of_alcacer_quibir.name: Battle of Alcácer Quibir (Battle of the Three Kings)
localization.event.battle_of_alcacer_quibir.desc: King Sebastian of Portugal invades Morocco to back a deposed Saadian claimant and is killed with much of the Portuguese nobility; the Saadian Ahmad al-Mansur becomes sultan.
localization.event.oman_expels_portuguese_from_muscat: The Ya'aruba imams take Muscat (1650), then raid Portuguese posts and capture Fort Jesus at Mombasa (1698) after a long siege.
localization.event.fall_of_isfahan.name: Afghan capture of Isfahan
localization.event.fall_of_isfahan.desc: Mahmud Hotak's Ghilzai Afghan army defeats the Safavids at Gulnabad and starves Isfahan into surrender; Shah Sultan Husayn abdicates. Russia and the Ottomans invade Iran's provinces.
localization.event.nader_shah_sacks_delhi.name: Nader Shah's invasion of India
localization.event.nader_shah_sacks_delhi.desc: Nader Shah, who expelled the Afghans and deposed the Safavids, defeats the Mughals at Karnal (1739), massacres part of Delhi's population and carries off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor.
localization.event.first_saudi_state.name: Pact of Diriyah and the first Saudi state
localization.event.first_saudi_state.desc: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab allies with Muhammad ibn Saud of Diriyah; the Emirate of Diriyah expands across Arabia and takes Mecca (1803-06) until destroyed by Muhammad Ali's Egyptian army (1818).
localization.event.treaty_of_kucuk_kaynarca.name: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca
localization.event.treaty_of_kucuk_kaynarca.desc: After defeat in the Russo-Turkish war of 1768-74 the Ottomans recognise Crimean independence (annexed by Russia 1783), open the Black Sea to Russian shipping and accept vague Russian protection claims over Orthodox Christians.
localization.event.qajar_dynasty_founded.name: Qajar reunification of Iran
localization.event.qajar_dynasty_founded.desc: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar defeats the Zands, sacks Tbilisi (1795) and is crowned shah in 1796 with Tehran as capital.
localization.event.french_invasion_of_egypt.name: French invasion of Egypt and Syria
localization.event.french_invasion_of_egypt.desc: Bonaparte defeats the Mamluk beys at the Pyramids; Nelson destroys the French fleet at Aboukir; the expedition fails at Acre and surrenders to British and Ottoman forces in 1801. Savants produce the Description de l'Égypte.
localization.event.muhammad_ali_takes_egypt.name: Muhammad Ali's Egypt
localization.event.muhammad_ali_takes_egypt.desc: An Albanian officer becomes Ottoman governor of Egypt, massacres the Mamluk beys (1811), builds a conscript army, state monopolies and factories, conquers Sudan (1820-22) and Syria (1831), and nearly defeats the sultan until Britain intervenes (1840).
localization.event.french_conquest_of_algeria.name: French conquest of Algeria
localization.event.french_conquest_of_algeria.desc: France takes Algiers in 1830; Emir Abd al-Qadir leads resistance until 1847, met with scorched-earth campaigns and massacres; settler colonisation follows and Algeria is annexed as French departments (1848).
localization.event.tanzimat.name: Tanzimat reforms
localization.event.tanzimat.desc: The Gülhane Rescript promises security of life and property, regular taxation and conscription; the 1856 Reform Edict declares equality of Muslims and non-Muslims. Builds on Mahmud II's abolition of the Janissaries (1826).
localization.event.suez_canal.name: Opening of the Suez Canal
localization.event.suez_canal.desc: Built by the French-led Suez Canal Company with Egyptian finance and forced (corvée) labour; shortens Europe-Asia sea routes by about 7,000 km.
localization.event.british_occupation_of_egypt.name: British occupation of Egypt
localization.event.british_occupation_of_egypt.desc: After state bankruptcy (1876), European debt control and the Urabi revolt against foreign influence, Britain bombards Alexandria and defeats Urabi at Tel el-Kebir, beginning a 'temporary' occupation that lasts until 1956.
localization.event.ottoman_constitution_1876.name: First Ottoman Constitution
localization.event.ottoman_constitution_1876.desc: Young Ottoman reformers obtain a constitution and parliament; Abdulhamid II suspends both during the Russo-Turkish war of 1877-78 and rules autocratically for 30 years.
localization.event.young_turk_revolution.name: Young Turk Revolution
localization.event.young_turk_revolution.desc: The Committee of Union and Progress forces Abdulhamid II to restore the constitution; after a 1909 counter-coup he is deposed; the CUP seizes full power in 1913.
localization.event.italian_invasion_of_libya.name: Italian invasion of Libya
localization.event.italian_invasion_of_libya.desc: Italy seizes Tripolitania and Cyrenaica (and the Dodecanese) from the Ottomans; Sanusi-led resistance continues until 1931-32, crushed with concentration camps in Cyrenaica.
localization.event.balkan_wars.name: Balkan Wars
localization.event.balkan_wars.desc: Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece and Montenegro drive the Ottomans from most of Europe; they then fight over Macedonia. Albania becomes independent. Large-scale civilian expulsions of Muslims and Christians.
localization.event.tongan_maritime_chiefdom.name: Tongan maritime chiefdom
localization.event.tongan_maritime_chiefdom.desc: The Tu'i Tonga paramount line, with the Tu'i Ha'atakalaua and later Tu'i Kanokupolu lines, maintains a network of political and marriage ties and exchange with Samoa, Fiji, 'Uvea and other islands.
localization.event.magellan_crosses_pacific.name: Magellan-Elcano circumnavigation
localization.event.magellan_crosses_pacific.desc: A Castilian expedition led by Magellan crosses the Pacific, touching Guam; Magellan is killed by Lapulapu's forces at Mactan (1521); Elcano returns with one ship.
localization.event.cook_voyages.name: Cook's Pacific voyages
localization.event.cook_voyages.desc: James Cook's three voyages chart New Zealand and eastern Australia (1770), with the help of the Ra'iatean navigator Tupaia, and reach Hawai'i, where Cook is killed in 1779.
localization.event.first_fleet.name: First Fleet and the colonisation of Australia
localization.event.first_fleet.desc: Eleven ships carrying about 1,500 people, mostly convicts, found a penal colony at Sydney Cove on Gadigal land under the doctrine later called terra nullius; smallpox devastates the Eora in 1789.
localization.event.hawaii_unification.name: Unification of Hawai'i
localization.event.hawaii_unification.desc: Kamehameha I, using Western firearms and advisers, conquers Maui, O'ahu (Nu'uanu 1795) and secures Kaua'i by agreement in 1810, founding the Kingdom of Hawai'i.
localization.event.musket_wars.name: Musket Wars
localization.event.musket_wars.desc: Inter-iwi wars in Aotearoa/New Zealand intensified by muskets acquired through trade (Ngāpuhi under Hongi Hika, Ngāti Toa under Te Rauparaha); tens of thousands die or are displaced.
localization.event.treaty_of_waitangi.name: Treaty of Waitangi
localization.event.treaty_of_waitangi.desc: British representatives and over 500 rangatira sign the treaty; the English text cedes sovereignty while the Māori text (te Tiriti) grants kawanatanga (governance) and guarantees tino rangatiratanga (full chieftainship).
localization.event.new_zealand_wars.name: New Zealand Wars
localization.event.new_zealand_wars.desc: Wars between the Crown, settlers and allied iwi on one side and Māori defending land and authority (Kīngitanga) on the other; Māori pā fortifications prove highly effective; the Crown confiscates about 1.2 million hectares (raupatu).
localization.event.blackbirding.name: Pacific labour trade (blackbirding)
localization.event.blackbirding.desc: About 60,000 Pacific Islanders, mainly from Vanuatu and the Solomon Islands, are recruited, often by deception or kidnapping, to work on Queensland sugar plantations; others go to Fiji, Samoa, New Caledonia and Peru (1862-63 Peruvian raids devastate Rapa Nui).
localization.event.overthrow_of_hawaiian_kingdom.name: Overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom
localization.event.overthrow_of_hawaiian_kingdom.desc: American and European sugar planters, backed by US Marines, depose Queen Lili'uokalani; the US annexes Hawai'i in 1898 despite petitions signed by most Native Hawaiians. The US apologised in 1993.
localization.event.australian_federation.name: Australian Federation
localization.event.australian_federation.desc: Six British colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia; one of the first acts is the Immigration Restriction Act (White Australia policy). Aboriginal people are excluded from the census until 1967.
localization.event.majapahit_collapse.name: Collapse of Majapahit and rise of Demak
localization.event.majapahit_collapse.desc: Majapahit fragments amid succession wars as Muslim port-states on Java's north coast, led by Demak, grow rich on trade with Malacca; by the 1520s the last Hindu-Buddhist court at Kediri/Daha is gone.
localization.event.portuguese_capture_of_malacca.name: Portuguese capture of Malacca
localization.event.portuguese_capture_of_malacca.desc: Albuquerque takes Malacca, the main entrepôt of the Straits; Sultan Mahmud Shah's court moves to Johor. Muslim traders shift to Aceh, Johor, Banten and Brunei.
localization.event.toungoo_conquests.name: Toungoo conquests under Bayinnaung
localization.event.toungoo_conquests.desc: Bayinnaung of Toungoo, using Portuguese mercenaries and firearms, conquers Pegu, the Shan states, Lan Na, Lan Xang and Ayutthaya (1564, 1569), creating the largest empire in mainland Southeast Asian history; it fragments after his death.
localization.event.spanish_philippines.name: Spanish colonisation of the Philippines
localization.event.spanish_philippines.desc: Miguel López de Legazpi establishes a Spanish base in Cebu (1565) and founds Manila (1571) after defeating Rajah Sulayman; Mindanao and Sulu sultanates resist for three centuries.
localization.event.manila_galleon_trade.name: Manila galleon trade
localization.event.manila_galleon_trade.desc: Annual galleons carry American silver from Acapulco to Manila and Chinese silks and porcelain back; Chinese (Sangley) merchants dominate Manila's economy.
localization.event.voc_founded.name: Founding of the Dutch East India Company
localization.event.voc_founded.desc: The States General charters the VOC with a monopoly on Dutch Asian trade and the power to wage war, make treaties and build forts; its tradable shares create the Amsterdam stock exchange.
localization.event.eic_founded.name: Founding of the English East India Company
localization.event.eic_founded.desc: Elizabeth I charters the 'Governor and Company of Merchants of London trading into the East Indies'; after losing the spice islands to the VOC it focuses on Indian textiles from Surat, Madras, Bombay and Calcutta.
localization.event.banda_conquest.name: VOC conquest of the Banda Islands
localization.event.banda_conquest.desc: Governor-General Jan Pieterszoon Coen's forces conquer the Banda Islands to monopolise nutmeg and mace; most of the population of perhaps 15,000 is killed, starved, enslaved or deported, and the land is worked by enslaved labour on perken plantations.
localization.event.burmese_sack_of_ayutthaya.name: Fall of Ayutthaya
localization.event.burmese_sack_of_ayutthaya.desc: Konbaung Burmese armies take and destroy Ayutthaya after a long siege; Taksin rallies resistance from Thonburi and expels the Burmese; the Chakri dynasty founds Bangkok (1782).
localization.event.voc_dissolved.name: Dissolution of the VOC
localization.event.voc_dissolved.desc: Bankrupt after the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War and the French conquest of the Netherlands, the VOC's charter lapses and its possessions pass to the Batavian state.
localization.event.first_anglo_burmese_war.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
localization.event.first_anglo_burmese_war.desc: Konbaung expansion into Assam and Manipur leads to war with the East India Company; Burma cedes Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim (Treaty of Yandabo). Further wars (1852, 1885) end the monarchy.
localization.event.java_war.name: Java War and the Cultivation System
localization.event.java_war.desc: Prince Diponegoro leads a revolt across central Java; about 200,000 Javanese die. After victory the Dutch impose the Cultivation System (1830), forcing villages to grow export crops.
localization.event.french_conquest_of_indochina.name: French conquest of Indochina
localization.event.french_conquest_of_indochina.desc: France attacks Da Nang (1858), annexes Cochinchina (1862-67), makes Cambodia a protectorate (1863), defeats Qing in the Sino-French War (1884-85) and forms the Indochinese Union (1887), adding Laos in 1893.
Siam accepts a British free-trade treaty with low tariffs and extraterritoriality (1855); King Chulalongkorn (r.1868-1910) centralises administration, abolishes slavery and corvée gradually, and cedes border territories to France and Britain to keep independence.
localization.event.aceh_war.name: Aceh War
localization.event.aceh_war.desc: The Netherlands invades the Aceh Sultanate; ulama-led guerrilla resistance lasts three decades and costs tens of thousands of lives, ended by van Heutsz's campaigns using Snouck Hurgronje's advice.
localization.event.philippine_revolution.name: Philippine Revolution and Philippine-American War
localization.event.philippine_revolution.desc: The Katipunan rises against Spain (1896); Aguinaldo declares independence (1898) during the Spanish-American War, but the US buys the Philippines in the Treaty of Paris and wins a brutal war (1899-1902) against the First Philippine Republic; hundreds of thousands of civilians die from violence, famine and disease.
localization.event.songhai_expansion.name: Sonni Ali's Songhai expansion
localization.event.songhai_expansion.desc: Sonni Ali turns Songhai into an empire, taking Timbuktu (1468) and Djenné (c.1473) from Mali's sphere and Tuareg control; Askia Muhammad (r.1493-1528) later expands it further and makes the hajj (1496-97).
localization.event.portuguese_elmina.name: Portuguese fort at Elmina
localization.event.portuguese_elmina.desc: Portugal builds São Jorge da Mina on the Gold Coast with the reluctant consent of the local ruler (Caramansa), gaining direct access to Akan gold; the Dutch take it in 1637.
localization.event.kongo_christianization.name: Christianization of Kongo
localization.event.kongo_christianization.desc: Manikongo Nzinga a Nkuwu is baptised (1491); his son Afonso I (r.1509-1542) wins the succession with Christian backing, builds a Kongolese Catholic church, exchanges embassies with Lisbon and Rome, and protests the slave trade's abuses in letters to João III.
