localization.event.portuguese_sugar_sao_tome.name: São Tomé sugar plantations
localization.event.portuguese_sugar_sao_tome.desc: Portuguese settlers on uninhabited São Tomé build sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans from Kongo and Benin; an enslaved revolt led by Amador (1595) shakes the colony.
localization.event.portuguese_raid_on_kilwa.name: Portuguese assault on the Swahili coast
localization.event.portuguese_raid_on_kilwa.desc: Francisco de Almeida's fleet sacks Kilwa and Mombasa (1505) to control the gold trade from Sofala and Indian Ocean shipping; Malindi allies with Portugal.
localization.event.battle_of_shimbra_kure.name: Adal invasion of Ethiopia
localization.event.battle_of_shimbra_kure.desc: Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi of Adal defeats Emperor Lebna Dengel at Shimbra Kure and overruns most of the Christian highlands, burning churches and monasteries.
localization.event.battle_of_wayna_daga.name: Battle of Wayna Daga
localization.event.battle_of_wayna_daga.desc: Emperor Gelawdewos, aided by Portuguese musketeers under Cristóvão da Gama (killed 1542), defeats and kills Imam Ahmad; Adal's conquest collapses.
localization.event.oromo_migrations.name: Oromo expansion
localization.event.oromo_migrations.desc: Oromo groups organised by the gadaa age-grade system move north into territories weakened by the Ethiopian-Adal war, settling much of southern and central Ethiopia and later integrating into the Gondarine state.
localization.event.battle_of_tondibi.name: Moroccan conquest of Songhai
localization.event.battle_of_tondibi.desc: Ahmad al-Mansur sends a musket-armed army of about 4,000 (many Iberian renegades) across the Sahara; it routs Askia Ishaq II at Tondibi and occupies Gao and Timbuktu, deporting scholars including Ahmad Baba.
localization.event.portuguese_luanda_founded.name: Founding of Portuguese Angola
localization.event.portuguese_luanda_founded.desc: Paulo Dias de Novais founds Luanda and begins wars of conquest against Ndongo, supported by Imbangala mercenaries; Angola becomes a colony organised around slave exports to Brazil.
localization.event.njinga_resistance.name: Queen Njinga's resistance
localization.event.njinga_resistance.desc: Njinga Mbande negotiates with Portugal (1622), takes power in Ndongo, conquers Matamba, allies with the Dutch during their occupation of Luanda (1641-48) and wages decades of war before a 1656 peace.
localization.event.battle_of_mbwila.name: Battle of Mbwila
localization.event.battle_of_mbwila.desc: Portuguese Angolan forces defeat and kill King António I of Kongo; Kongo collapses into civil wars until Pedro IV's restoration (1709), helped by the Antonian movement of Dona Beatriz Kimpa Vita (executed 1706).
localization.event.rise_of_asante.name: Rise of Asante
localization.event.rise_of_asante.desc: Osei Tutu and the priest Okomfo Anokye unite Akan states around the Golden Stool; Asante defeats Denkyira at Feyiase (1701) and under Opoku Ware expands into a large empire trading gold, kola and captives.
localization.event.dahomey_conquers_whydah.name: Dahomey conquers Allada and Whydah
localization.event.dahomey_conquers_whydah.desc: King Agaja of Dahomey conquers the coastal kingdoms of Allada (1724) and Hueda/Whydah (1727), gaining direct access to European slave traders; Dahomey becomes a tributary of Oyo (1730-1823).
localization.event.futa_jallon_jihad.name: Futa Jallon jihad
localization.event.futa_jallon_jihad.desc: Fulbe Muslim clerics and allies establish an imamate in the Futa Jallon highlands (Guinea) under the almami, with a council of provinces; Futa Toro follows (1776).
localization.event.sokoto_jihad.name: Sokoto jihad
localization.event.sokoto_jihad.desc: Usman dan Fodio's hijra from Gobir begins a jihad that overthrows the Hausa kings; the Sokoto Caliphate, with emirates such as Kano and Zaria under a caliph, becomes the largest state in 19th-century West Africa.
localization.event.rise_of_the_zulu_kingdom.name: Rise of the Zulu kingdom
localization.event.rise_of_the_zulu_kingdom.desc: Shaka builds the Zulu kingdom from the Mthethwa confederacy, defeating the Ndwandwe (1819) and reorganising age regiments; assassinated in 1828.
localization.event.great_trek.name: Great Trek
localization.event.great_trek.desc: Several thousand Afrikaner Voortrekkers leave the British Cape, partly over the abolition of slavery and frontier policy, fight the Ndebele and Zulu (Blood River 1838) and found the Natalia, Orange Free State and Transvaal republics.
localization.event.british_abolition_of_slave_trade.n: British abolition of the slave trade
localization.event.british_abolition_of_slave_trade.d: Parliament bans the British slave trade after a mass petitioning campaign, Quaker and Black abolitionists (Equiano, Cugoano) and the shock of the Haitian Revolution; the Royal Navy's West Africa Squadron (1808) later intercepts slavers. The US bans imports from 1808.
localization.event.berlin_conference.name: Berlin Conference
localization.event.berlin_conference.desc: Fourteen states, with no African representatives, set rules for 'effective occupation' of African coasts, recognise Leopold II's Congo Free State and declare free trade on the Congo and Niger.
localization.event.congo_free_state_atrocities.name: Congo Free State atrocities
localization.event.congo_free_state_atrocities.desc: Leopold II's private colony forces Congolese people to collect wild rubber under quotas enforced by hostage-taking, mutilation and killing by the Force Publique; exposed by Morel, Casement and Congolese testimony, Belgium annexes it in 1908.
localization.event.battle_of_adwa.name: Battle of Adwa
localization.event.battle_of_adwa.desc: Emperor Menelik II's army, well supplied with modern rifles and artillery, decisively defeats an Italian invasion force; Italy recognises Ethiopian independence (Treaty of Addis Ababa).
localization.event.herero_and_nama_genocide.name: Herero and Nama genocide
localization.event.herero_and_nama_genocide.desc: After Herero and Nama uprisings against land seizures in German South West Africa, General von Trotha's extermination order and concentration camps kill an estimated majority of the Herero and around half of the Nama. Germany acknowledged it as genocide in 2021.
localization.event.maji_maji_rebellion.name: Maji Maji rebellion
localization.event.maji_maji_rebellion.desc: Peoples of southern German East Africa rise against forced cotton cultivation, united by the maji (water) medicine; German scorched-earth tactics cause a famine killing perhaps 75,000-300,000.
localization.event.british_conquest_of_sokoto.name: British conquest of the Sokoto Caliphate
localization.event.british_conquest_of_sokoto.desc: Lugard's West African Frontier Force takes Kano and Sokoto; Caliph Attahiru I flees east and is killed at Burmi. Emirs are retained under 'indirect rule'.
localization.event.world_war_i.name: First World War
localization.event.world_war_i.desc: After the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo (28 June 1914), Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia with German backing; Russia, France and Britain enter within a week, the Ottoman Empire joins the Central Powers (November 1914), Italy the Entente (1915) and the USA (April 1917). Besides the Western and Eastern fronts, the war is fought at Gallipoli, in Mesopotamia, Sinai-Palestine and the Caucasus, in Togo, Kamerun, South West Africa and a four-year East African campaign, and at Tsingtao and the German Pacific islands. Britain draws about 1.4 million Indian soldiers and Dominion forces (Australia, New Zealand, Canada, South Africa); France recruits about half a million colonial troops including some 170,000-200,000 West African tirailleurs; about 140,000 Chinese labourers serve in France; hundreds of thousands of African porters are conscripted, and over 100,000 die in East Africa.
localization.event.armenian_genocide.name: Armenian Genocide
localization.event.armenian_genocide.desc: During the war the Committee of Union and Progress government (Talaat, Enver, Djemal) arrests and murders Armenian community leaders in Constantinople (from 24 April 1915), disarms and kills Armenian conscripts, and under the deportation law of May 1915 drives Armenian communities of Anatolia on death marches to the Syrian desert (Deir ez-Zor), with mass killings by the Special Organization, gendarmes and irregulars, starvation, abductions and forced conversion. Assyrian and Greek Orthodox communities are also targeted. Armenians resist at Van (April-May 1915) and Musa Dagh, where survivors are evacuated by French warships (September 1915).
localization.event.russian_revolution.name: Russian Revolution
localization.event.russian_revolution.desc: Bread riots and strikes in Petrograd, joined by the garrison, force Nicholas II to abdicate (March 1917, February by the old calendar); a Provisional Government coexists with the Petrograd Soviet and keeps fighting. In November (October Old Style) the Bolsheviks under Lenin seize power, decree peace and land redistribution, dissolve the Constituent Assembly (January 1918) and sign the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (3 March 1918), giving up Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland and Ukraine. Civil war with the Whites, foreign intervention and peasant and national revolts follows until about 1921.
localization.event.wilsonian_moment.name: The Wilsonian moment
localization.event.wilsonian_moment.desc: Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points (8 January 1918) and Lenin's calls for self-determination are read across the colonial world as a promise. Nationalists send delegations and petitions to the Paris Peace Conference, including Saad Zaghlul's Wafd from Egypt, Korean exiles and the young Nguyen Ai Quoc (Ho Chi Minh) for Vietnam. When the victors keep empires intact, 1919 brings the Egyptian revolution (March), the March First Movement in Korea, the Rowlatt satyagraha and the Amritsar (Jallianwala Bagh) massacre in India (13 April) and the May Fourth Movement in China.
localization.event.armistice_1918.name: Armistices of 1918
localization.event.armistice_1918.desc: After the failure of Germany's spring offensives and the Allied Hundred Days, Bulgaria signs an armistice at Salonica (29 September), the Ottomans at Mudros (30 October) and Austria-Hungary at Villa Giusti (3 November) as the Habsburg monarchy dissolves into Czechoslovakia, the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, Poland and Hungary. Naval mutiny at Kiel spreads into revolution in Germany; Wilhelm II abdicates (9 November) and the new republic signs the armistice at Compiègne on 11 November.
localization.event.influenza_pandemic_1918.name: Influenza pandemic of 1918-1920
localization.event.influenza_pandemic_1918.desc: An H1N1 influenza spreads along troop, shipping and rail routes in three waves; the deadliest, in autumn 1918, kills young adults especially. British India loses perhaps 12-14 million people, far more than any other country; in New Zealand-administered Western Samoa, the ship Talune brings the virus in November 1918 and about a fifth of the population dies, while quarantined American Samoa records no deaths. Mortality is very high in southern Africa, among Indigenous communities in Alaska and Labrador, and in Iran.
localization.event.treaty_of_versailles.name: Treaty of Versailles
localization.event.treaty_of_versailles.desc: At the Paris Peace Conference the victors impose terms on Germany without negotiation; the treaty is signed on 28 June 1919. Germany loses Alsace-Lorraine, territory to Poland including a corridor to the sea, and all colonies, which become League of Nations mandates (Tanganyika, Kamerun, Togo, South West Africa, New Guinea, Samoa and the Pacific islands north of the equator). Article 231 assigns war responsibility as the basis for reparations, fixed in 1921 at 132 billion gold marks. The Covenant creates the League of Nations; Japan's racial equality proposal is blocked and German rights in Shandong go to Japan.
localization.event.may_fourth_movement.name: May Fourth Movement
localization.event.may_fourth_movement.desc: About 3,000 Beijing students march from Tiananmen on 4 May 1919 against the Paris decision to give Germany's Shandong rights to Japan, and burn the house of a pro-Japanese minister. Arrests spark strikes by Shanghai workers and merchants and boycotts of Japanese goods; three officials are dismissed and the Chinese delegation refuses to sign the Treaty of Versailles. The protest merges with the New Culture Movement's attack on Confucian tradition and its call for vernacular literature, science and democracy.
localization.event.may_fourth_movement.option.strikes: Strikes boycott and refusal to sign
localization.event.soviet_union_founded.name: Founding of the Soviet Union
localization.event.soviet_union_founded.desc: After the Red Army wins the civil war and reconquers Ukraine, the Caucasus and much of Central Asia, the Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian and Transcaucasian Soviet republics sign the treaty creating the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. Lenin's federal model with a nominal right of secession prevails over Stalin's plan to absorb the republics into Russia; real power lies with the single Communist Party. The New Economic Policy (1921) restores small private trade; korenizatsiia promotes non-Russian languages and elites.
localization.event.treaty_of_lausanne.name: Treaty of Lausanne
localization.event.treaty_of_lausanne.desc: Mustafa Kemal's nationalist government in Ankara rejects the Treaty of Sevres (1920) and, after defeating Greek forces in Anatolia (1922), French forces in Cilicia and Armenian forces in the east, abolishes the sultanate (November 1922). At Lausanne the Allies recognise Turkey's borders and abolish the capitulations; a convention of January 1923 makes compulsory the exchange of about 1.2 million Orthodox Christians from Anatolia and about 400,000 Muslims from Greece. The Arab provinces remain under British and French mandates; the Kurds receive no state. The Republic of Turkey is proclaimed on 29 October 1923.
localization.event.great_depression.name: Great Depression
localization.event.great_depression.desc: The Wall Street crash of October 1929 and the collapse of US lending turn a downturn into a world depression, transmitted by the gold standard, banking crises (Austria's Creditanstalt and Germany in 1931) and protection (Smoot-Hawley tariff, 1930). World trade falls by about two-thirds in value by 1933; US unemployment reaches about a quarter of the workforce and German unemployment about six million. Prices of coffee, rubber, sugar, cocoa, rice and wheat collapse, ruining exporters from Brazil and Argentina to the Gold Coast, Malaya, Java and Burma, where the Saya San peasant rebellion breaks out (1930-32). Military coups follow in Argentina and Brazil (1930) and elsewhere in Latin America.
localization.event.italian_invasion_of_ethiopia.name: Italian invasion of Ethiopia
localization.event.italian_invasion_of_ethiopia.desc: Using the Walwal incident (December 1934) as pretext, Fascist Italy invades Ethiopia from Eritrea and Italian Somaliland. The League of Nations names Italy the aggressor and imposes sanctions, but not on oil, and Britain keeps the Suez Canal open; the Hoare-Laval plan to cede much of Ethiopia leaks and collapses. Italian forces use mustard gas against soldiers and civilians and take Addis Ababa on 5 May 1936; Haile Selassie goes into exile and addresses the League in Geneva (30 June 1936). Patriot (Arbegnoch) resistance continues; after an attempt on Viceroy Graziani, Italian forces massacre thousands in Addis Ababa (Yekatit 12, February 1937) and later the monks of Debre Libanos. Ethiopian patriots, Sudanese, Indian, African and South African troops under British command liberate the country in 1941.
localization.event.italian_invasion_of_ethiopia.optio: Resist and appeal to the league
localization.event.second_sino_japanese_war.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
localization.event.second_sino_japanese_war.desc: Six years after seizing Manchuria (1931) and creating Manchukuo, Japan turns a clash at the Marco Polo Bridge near Beijing into full-scale war. Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists fight at Shanghai (August-November 1937); Japanese troops take Nanjing in December 1937 and kill tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of prisoners and civilians, with mass rape. To slow the Japanese advance the Nationalists breach the Yellow River dikes (June 1938), drowning or starving hundreds of thousands of Chinese peasants. The government retreats to Chongqing; a fragile United Front with the Communists holds in name. Japan's occupation brings the 'Three Alls' campaigns in North China, bombing of cities, chemical and biological warfare (Unit 731), and forced labour from Korea, Taiwan and occupied China.
localization.event.second_sino_japanese_war.option.to: Total resistance trading space for time
